thread:
Sam: Heads-up: saw a sharp apiserver connection and etcd tail latency spike in eu-west-2 at ~09:14 UTC. p95->p99 jump and a lot of dial timeouts.
OpsBot: alert: apiserver.p99_rpc_latency > 600ms (eu-west-2)
Leila: any deploys or CI around then?
Sam: nothing in apps, but provisioning showed a mass of new GPU nodes being initialized by the autoscaler pool. Lots of init containers running early setup scripts.
Diego: init containers often open ephemeral HTTP connections to the control plane for readiness/annotation. If they all retry aggressively you can get a syn-flood-like connection churn.
Mei: dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/controlplane -> apiserver_conn_count, etcd_tail_latency, controllermanager_lease_renew_failures. controller-manager lease-renew errors spiked too.
Sam: apiserver log excerpt:
```
I0319 09:14:12.112 server.go:438] http2: active_conns=1120 in_flight=210 p99_etcd=920ms
E0319 09:14:12.998 round_trippers.go:245] dial tcp 10.40.2.11:2379: i/o timeout
E0319 09:14:13.201 cacher.go:398] kvcache miss: /nodes/gpu-setup-239
```
Leila: controller-manager backoffs indicate lease writes couldn't complete timely. That will cascade to leader election jitter for controllers.
Diego: network side — check node conntrack counters and NAT gateway metrics. If conntrack table or SNAT ports exhaust, clients will hang and retry.
Mei: SNAT ports for the NAT GW didn't max out but the per-node conntrack entries were near the limit on multiple worker nodes.
Sam: interesting — so it's local conntrack, not global NAT. That suggests the init scripts are creating many short-lived connections from each node.
Diego: we also saw high kvcache invalidations. When pods rapidly register/unregister, prefix invalidation causes re-listing which amplifies etcd reads.
Leila: short-term: increase nf_conntrack_max and reduce nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait on the affected nodes. Also add randomized jitter to the provisioner so only N drivers install concurrently per node.
Mei: I've prepared a quick canary patch to the driver-installer to limit concurrency to 8 and add exponential backoff on 5xx/timeout. Will roll to staging first.
Sam: mitigation steps I'm applying now:
```
# bump conntrack
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-eu-west-2 -o name); do ssh $n sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000; done
# reduce TIME_WAIT to free ports faster
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-eu-west-2 -o name); do ssh $n sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30; done
```
Diego: can we also add a short-lived sidecar cache for the provisioner so it uses local list results instead of hammering apiserver for every init step? That'd reduce kvcache churn.
Leila: agreed — follow-up: design a prefix-aware cache with TTL and a small invalidation window. Add to roadmap SRE-8120.
Mei: cost/ops note: bumping conntrack is cheap but fragile; if we don't fix provisioning behavior we'll keep paying hands-on response time.
Sam: timeline: 1) apply sysctl bump + tcp timeout (now) 2) patch provisioner concurrency/backoff (canary in 15m) 3) implement local pre-warm/list caching (design ticket) 4) long-term: tune apiserver watcher fanout if we see sustained burst patterns.
Diego: I'll run a quick experiment to replay a scaled-down onboarding in staging and capture conntrack growth to validate the fix.
Mei: PR link for canary: https://github.com/redwood/provisioner/pull/218 — includes jitter and concurrency cap.
Leila: I'll open SRE ticket SRE-8120 and include cost roughs and runbook for rollback.
OpsBot: created ticket SRE-8120 "init-container connection churn causing apiserver tail latency during GPU onboarding"
Sam: excellent. Monitor p99_etcd, apiserver_conn_count, conntrack_used. If any metric crosses thresholds rollback the canary.
Leila: adding thresholds: apiserver_conn_count > 900 or p99_etcd > 800ms => rollback.
Mei: rolling canary now to 5% of nodes.
Diego: running staging replay now. will report results in 20m.
Sam: thanks team. keep updates brief here. :coffee:
